issues.detail: The Greek 'σταυρωσον' (crucify) is an imperative. The Vietnamese translation 'Hãy đóng đinh nó!' adds the pronoun 'nó' (it/him), which is not present in the Greek text.

The Greek 'λαβετε αυτον υμεις και σταυρωσατε' means 'Take him yourselves and crucify [him]'. The Vietnamese 'Các ngươi hãy bắt lấy Ngài mà đóng đinh đi' uses 'mà' which can imply 'in order to', but the Greek structure is a compound command (take and crucify). More importantly, the Vietnamese adds 'đi' as a final particle which is not in the Greek.
